meta.title: Investigation Ontology (Demo)
meta.description: A minimal vocabulary for AML investigation records, built to demonstrate how business data can point into AMLO and AMLTRIX. An extension: not part of AMLO or AMLTRIX.
meta.note: Not a standard and not complete. The namespace is a placeholder.

classes.label: Alert
classes.comment: A flag raised by monitoring (a rule, a model or a graph analysis) on some activity.

classes.label: Case
classes.comment: An investigation opened on one or more alerts.

classes.label: Checklist item
classes.comment: One suggested line of enquiry for an alert: an AMLTRIX indicator to look into, why it matters for this alert, how urgent it is, and which kind of records would show it. Advice only: no data is queried.

classes.label: Evidence
classes.comment: A piece of material gathered for an alert or case. Its kind is given by inv:recordType, an AMLTRIX data source type.

classes.label: Finding
classes.comment: An investigator's assessment of one AMLTRIX indicator within a case.

classes.label: Paragraph
classes.comment: One paragraph of a report draft, tied to the findings it rests on.

classes.label: Report draft
classes.comment: A draft narrative for a case. It always requires investigator review.

properties.label: based on
properties.comment: The findings a paragraph rests on.

properties.label: hypothesis
properties.comment: An AMLTRIX technique the case is investigating.

properties.label: indicator
properties.comment: The AMLTRIX indicator a checklist item or finding is about.

properties.label: paragraphs
properties.comment: The ordered paragraphs of a report draft (an rdf:List).

properties.label: record type
properties.comment: The kind of record the evidence is: an AMLTRIX data source.

properties.label: suggested data source
properties.comment: An AMLTRIX data source (a type of record) the investigator should look at for the indicator.

properties.label: suspected technique
properties.comment: The AMLTRIX technique an alert is suspected to involve. A hypothesis, not a conclusion.

properties.label: technique
properties.comment: The AMLTRIX technique a finding is made under.

properties.label: fact
properties.comment: One fact the monitoring systems attached to the alert, as plain text: a rule that fired, a model score, a cycle with its payments.

properties.label: priority
properties.comment: Order in which to look into the suggestions for one alert. 1 is first.

properties.label: reason
properties.comment: Why this indicator is worth checking for this alert, in the adviser's words. Advice, not a finding.

properties.label: source id
properties.comment: The identifier the record has in the source system.

properties.label: status
properties.comment: Whether the indicator was supported, not supported, inconclusive, or could not be assessed.

properties.label: trigger reason
properties.comment: Why the monitoring system raised the alert, as stated by that system.

rules.message: An alert needs exactly one alert id.
An alert needs exactly one raised-at timestamp (xsd:dateTime).

rules.rule: at least one, of type xsd:string
rules.message: An alert needs the reason the monitoring system raised it.

rules.rule: at least one, pointing to amlo:Technique
rules.message: An alert needs at least one suspected technique, and it must be an AMLTRIX technique.
hasEvidence must point to Evidence.
A case needs exactly one case id.
A case needs exactly one opened-at timestamp.

rules.rule: at least one, pointing to amlo:Technique
rules.message: A case needs at least one hypothesis, and it must be an AMLTRIX technique.
A checklist item belongs to exactly one alert.
A checklist item is about exactly one AMLTRIX indicator.

rules.rule: exactly one, of type xsd:integer, at least 1
rules.message: A checklist item needs exactly one priority, a whole number from 1 upwards.
A checklist item needs a reason why the indicator matters for this alert.

rules.rule: at least one, pointing to amlo:DataSource
rules.message: A checklist item must suggest at least one data source to look at, and it must be an AMLTRIX data source.
Evidence needs exactly one record type, and it must be an AMLTRIX data source.
A finding is made under exactly one AMLTRIX technique.
A finding is about exactly one AMLTRIX indicator.

rules.rule: exactly one, one of: supported, not-supported, inconclusive, not-assessable
rules.message: status must be supported, not-supported, inconclusive or not-assessable.

rules.rule: at least one, of type xsd:string
rules.message: A finding needs an observation.
A supported finding must cite the evidence it rests on.
A paragraph needs exactly one text.

rules.rule: at least one, pointing to inv:Finding
rules.message: Every paragraph must be based on at least one finding.
A report draft belongs to exactly one case.
A report draft needs a review status.
A report draft needs one ordered list of paragraphs.

consistency: a checklist item's indicator does not belong to the alert's suspected technique
a checklist item suggests a data source that AMLTRIX does not list for the alert's suspected technique
a finding's indicator does not belong to the finding's technique
a finding is made under a technique the case is not investigating
a report paragraph rests on a finding that is not part of the report's case

@graph.trigger_reason: Graph analysis: payment 5007762 closes a verified time-ordered cycle of 3 payments that returns to the originating account within 6.92 days
facts: Rule engine: rule_money_mule fired. What this rule detects: An inflow of at least $3,000 followed within 3 days by an outflow of at least 85% of it from the same account (rapid pass-through).
Rule engine: rule_high_risk_country fired. What this rule detects: Payment currency is Ruble or Mexican Peso, used as a jurisdiction proxy because the dataset has no country field.
ML model: score 0.695. The model gives a probability and names no reason.

Transaction graph: this payment closes a verified time-ordered cycle of 3 payments that returns to the originating account 8060BA880, over 6.92 days. The payments: 2022-09-03 17:09 8060BA880 to 8060A62F0 68,647.24; 2022-09-08 15:50 8060A62F0 to 8060AF460 100,578.47; 2022-09-10 15:19 8060AF460 to 8060BA880 196,999.50.
The payment: 196,999.50 Ruble by ACH, from 8060AF460 to 8060BA880 on 2022-09-10 15:19. Cross-currency: no. Same bank: no. Between the same account: no.

@graph.reason: The graph found a verified cycle that returns to the originating account, which is the core of this indicator.
Three accounts form the ring, which raises the question of who owns them and when they were opened.
The payment currency is Ruble, which the rule engine treats as a high-risk jurisdiction proxy; the routing of the ring is worth checking.

@graph.observation: In the transaction log, 3 payments take funds from 8060BA880 through 2 other accounts and back to it within 6.92 days: 8060BA880 to 8060A62F0 68,647.24; 8060A62F0 to 8060AF460 100,578.47; 8060AF460 to 8060BA880 196,999.50.
Ownership and onboarding records were not part of this case's evidence, so this indicator was not assessed.
The payment currency is Ruble, which the rule engine treats as a proxy for a high-risk country, but the data has no country field, so cross-border routing could not be assessed.

paragraphs.text: Transaction records show funds leaving account 8060BA880 and returning to it within 6.92 days, consistent with Circular Transactions (T0039) and indicator IND02191; the last payment is 196,999.50 Ruble.
Indicators IND02194 and IND02195 could not be assessed, because ownership records and country data were not available.
